# ada-url / idna

ada-url's own fuzz target `idna` ([source](source/idna.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over ada (ada-url/ada at e6754478).

to_unicode(to_ascii(x)), UTF-8<->UTF-32 transcoding round trip, label validation, mapping and normalisation are computed but never compared (the source comment says equality is deliberately not asserted).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against ada at commit e6754478.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- to_ascii(to_ascii(x)) == to_ascii(x) whenever the first result is non-empty and the second is non-empty (an empty second result is excused) ([lines 172-183](source/idna.cc#L172-L183)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- to_unicode(to_unicode(x)) == to_unicode(x) whenever both are non-empty ([lines 192-203](source/idna.cc#L192-L203)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Punycode: d = punycode_to_utf32(blob); if utf32_to_punycode(d) succeeds and re-decoding succeeds, the re-decoded code points equal d (a failing re-decode is not flagged) ([lines 236-256](source/idna.cc#L236-L256)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch ada-url` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `idna.plain` | 660,136 | `002abc860665462e29a3ce5d64feb663f3dd6867fc236b1ac0eaac706426fbd8` |
| ubsan | `idna.ubsan` | 720,312 | `89cb428b040d72cae0a83298f2823e613839a9fcdfd8571cad9d2ab1591b4817` |
| asan | `idna.asan` | 1,539,928 | `346b30625cb494a4a37b437b7e62bf240f0e160a7fde1ffa284b8ec7f72c45b0` |
| asan-ubsan | `idna.asan-ubsan` | 1,602,296 | `437a274e14c7c3dfa1fd434239a0f6202126474df1dd50b62ee40401e50e6477` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
